reason: This narrative (Judges 4) does not support the claim that regular people should not complain to their leaders. In fact, the Israelites appropriately come to Deborah, their judge, for judgment (וַיַּעֲלוּ אֵלֶיהָ בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל לַמִּשְׁפָּט - 'the children of Israel came up to her for judgment'), which is presented as normal and proper governance. Additionally, when the people cry out (וַיִּצְעֲקוּ), they cry out to God (אֶל־יְהוָה), not to complain to their leaders, and this cry is divinely answered. The narrative portrays Deborah's leadership as legitimate and her response as just. There is no moral message discouraging people from seeking justice or guidance from their leaders; rather, the text validates both proper appeals to judges and cries to God during oppression.
